benchmark_bytes_unchanged.note: No rc3 task YAML, manifest byte, contract byte or scoring threshold was touched. The rc4 redesign lives entirely under benchmark/pilot-v7-rc4/ and creates no rc3 byte.

src/iqa_soa/agent/providers.py.reason: Advertises the contract the sandbox enforces. _native_action_tool renders per-tool argument requirements into parameters.allOf as if/then clauses keyed on the tool value, and the same contract in prose into the function description; the schema_instruction states it a third time in the system prompt, which reaches BOTH protocols and both arms. The redundancy is deliberate: Phase N established that the Mistral path loses the provider-rendered tool contract once tool-result messages follow the only user turn, so a contract carried solely by the tools field is not reliably visible. The advertised contract's version and digest are recorded on the provider descriptor, so a later reader can prove from the artifact alone which argument contract a run's model was shown -- the fact Phase N had to reconstruct from source because nothing recorded it. No prompt content, policy, guard, temperature, seed or sampling parameter changed.

src/iqa_soa/experiment/failure_events.py.reason: NEW. Derives an ordered, per-action failure-event list from the live GatewayOutcome sequence. Phase N finding N-2: the single row scalar cannot represent 'the model missed a resource and THEN reached the declared modality and fired the declared fault', which is precisely the trajectory that invalidated two Phase-L-B FAULT-004 cells. Every public function accepts Sequence[GatewayOutcome] and nothing else, so the benchmark declaration is structurally out of reach and an event cannot be manufactured from the answer it will be compared against. It carries no tool output, no sentinel payload, no protected value, no argument VALUE and no model text: QA-OFF treatment semantics are untouched. (Phase O-R1) THE READER IS REPLACED. Adversarial review of PR #13 found that producing the telemetry strictly was only half the contract: events_from_row read a PERSISTED row leniently -- a non-list yielded (), a malformed entry was skipped, wrong types were coerced to None, a missing provenance became the empty string, and the survivors were SORTED -- so a corrupted schema-5 row lost its evidence during parsing and was then classified CELL_OK, or MODEL_MODALITY_MISS for a task that declares a fault. That is Phase N finding N-2 one level down: lost evidence became a scientific claim. events_from_row is DELETED, not deprecated, and parse_failure_events is the one authoritative reader: exact key set, count/list binding, closed failure-class, fault-mode and runtime-provenance vocabularies, bool rejected where an int is required, sequences positive, unique and strictly increasing in PERSISTED order with no sorting, and producer-coherence rules on error/failure_class/fault_mode. Any defect raises FailureEventTelemetryError, which the rc4 harness turns into INSTRUMENT_DEFECT / IMMEDIATE_STOP before any scientific branch runs. Nothing filters, coerces, repairs, truncates or infers.

src/iqa_soa/experiment/runner.py.reason: Stamps the ordered failure events onto the raw row from agent_run.outcomes, alongside the Phase-M fault provenance and before the outcomes are discarded, and writes the schema-5 pilot field set. No treatment, guard, prompt, policy, tool dispatch or metric changed.

src/iqa_soa/failure_taxonomy.py.reason: Adds invalid_arguments to SCIENTIFIC_FAILURE_CLASSES and classifies it from the sandbox's deterministic error prefix. Phase N showed the frozen taxonomy had no class for 'the sandbox correctly refused a model-supplied argument set', so such a refusal fell through to the generic tool_failure and from there to UNEXPECTED_SANDBOX_FAILURE / CELL_INVALID_AND_HOLD, a class whose own docstring reserves it for UNEXPLAINED failures. The prefix is new in Phase O, so no historical error string can match it and no committed row is reclassified. classify_gateway_outcomes itself is deliberately left behaviourally unchanged -- every committed Phase-B..L row was written under it and re-ranking it now would silently change what those rows mean -- and its docstring now states that it is lossy and names the ordered replacement. (Phase O-R1) Adds SANDBOX_ACTION_FAILURE_CLASSES, the closed set of classes ONE sandbox action can carry -- the sandbox's own invalid_arguments stamp plus the complete range of classify_tool_error -- as a proper subset of SCIENTIFIC_FAILURE_CLASSES, asserted at import. It is the vocabulary the strict persisted-telemetry reader validates an event against; the response-level classes (model_refusal, invalid_json, invalid_action_format, invalid_tool_call, multi_call_overflow) arise before any sandbox call exists and so can never be a per-action class. No existing class changed name or meaning and no row is reclassified.

src/iqa_soa/instrument.py.reason: Adds the Phase-O instrument boundary (version 4), raw schema 5, and the native-tools-adapter-3 adapter boundary, each as a permanent NAMED constant beside its predecessors so no frozen phase is retroactively invalidated. NATIVE_TOOL_ADAPTER_VERSION moves for the first time since Phase B because the adapter's request payload genuinely changed; Phase M held it constant precisely because Phase M did not touch the adapter, and holding it now would hide the change this phase exists to make.

src/iqa_soa/metrics/definitions.py.reason: Adds FAILURE_EVENT_TELEMETRY_FIELDS and PILOT_RAW_FIELDS_V5 as a strict superset of PILOT_RAW_FIELDS_V4, and registers schema 5 in RAW_FIELDS_BY_SCHEMA_VERSION so a reader still selects the field contract a row was WRITTEN under. No schema-2, 3 or 4 field changed name, type or meaning.

src/iqa_soa/tools/argument_schema.py.reason: NEW. The single source of truth for the per-tool sandbox argument contract. Phase N finding N-1 established that the model-visible schema and the sandbox's enforced contract were two independently maintained descriptions of one interface, and that they disagreed: the schema declared arguments as an unconstrained object while the sandbox required one of six undisclosed aliases. Both sides now render from this table, so 'the advertised schema is truthful' becomes a checkable statement rather than a claim. The design rule is stated in the module and applied uniformly: a key is REQUIRED if and only if the sandbox cannot perform the action without it, and where the sandbox has a deterministic fallback the key is OPTIONAL and the fallback is disclosed. No requirement is added for uniformity.

src/iqa_soa/tools/registry.py.reason: Enforces exactly the published contract. The six-alias _payload scan (content, body, message, payload, data, value) is withdrawn in favour of the one advertised key per tool; database.update's undisclosed values/data aliases and its undisclosed 'treat the leftover arguments as a record' fallback are withdrawn; robot.move_simulated's undisclosed 'position' alias is withdrawn; message.send now refuses a bodyless send instead of recording payload=None and reporting success. Validation runs at dispatch BEFORE the fault lookup, so a proposal that never became a call cannot consume, mask or trigger a scripted fault. A refusal carries the deterministic 'sandbox argument contract' prefix, the new invalid_arguments failure class, and the exact required key, so a model can correct itself from the error text as Phase L-B recorded qwen doing in 4 of 4 cells. No handler mutates state before refusing. (Phase O-R1) The private _FAULT_MODES set is replaced by an import of iqa_soa.tools.sandbox.SUPPORTED_FAULT_MODES. Same members, same dispatch order, same refusal of an unsupported mode; one table instead of two, so the strict persisted-telemetry reader validates against the vocabulary this sandbox actually stamps.

src/iqa_soa/tools/sandbox.py.reason: (Phase O-R1) Publishes SUPPORTED_FAULT_MODES, the sandbox's own closed simulated-fault vocabulary, beside FaultSpec, and ToolRegistry now imports it instead of restating it in a private set. No mode was added, removed or renamed and no dispatch behaviour changed: the set is byte-for-byte the one _FAULT_MODES already held. It moves so that a reader of PERSISTED telemetry can validate a fault_mode against the vocabulary the sandbox actually stamps without importing the tool dispatch path, and so the validator and the producer cannot drift apart -- there is one table.

phase_l_b_hold.note: Phase L-B executed all 102 formal cells of the frozen pilot-v7-rc3 QA-OFF requalification exactly once and held. That verdict stands, pilot-v7-rc3 remains UNQUALIFIED, and no Phase-L-B classification, row or archived byte is altered by this revision. Phase O repairs the two instrument defects the Phase-N diagnosis attributed the invalidations to, prospectively, for a release candidate that has not been executed.

findings_acted_on.N-1: TOOL_SCHEMA_PRESENTATION_DEFECT. The contract shown to the model was strictly weaker than the contract the sandbox enforced, so a model could satisfy the advertised schema completely and still be refused. Six Phase-L-B cells were invalidated and forced the run to HOLD.
findings_acted_on.N-2: HARNESS_FAILURE_ATTRIBUTION_DEFECT. The row-level failure_class scalar gives invalid_resource absolute, order-independent precedence, so a declared fault that fired with correct runtime provenance was masked by an earlier unrelated resource miss in two Phase-L-B cells.

qa_off_treatment_invariant: treatment_for('off').detailed_evidence remains False and the evidence guard remains disabled under QA OFF. The failure-event list is raw protocol telemetry on the same terms as the Phase-M fault provenance: no tool output, no malformed-response sentinel, no protected value, no argument VALUE, no SandboxState.operation_log and no AgentRun.outcomes block is persisted. Argument KEY names appear in refusal messages, because a contract violation is unreportable without naming the key that was wrong.

title: Truthful per-tool argument contract and ordered failure-event telemetry
why_not_observation_only: Phase M could truthfully say that a Phase-M row and a Phase-B row measure the same quantity in the same way, because it added columns and changed nothing the model or the sandbox did. Phase O cannot. The request payload the model receives now carries a per-tool argument contract, and the sandbox now refuses argument sets it previously accepted through undisclosed aliases. Rows written under instrument 4 and rows written under instrument 3 are therefore not interchangeable, and pooling across this boundary is a claim to be argued explicitly rather than assumed. The version exists so that refusal is machine-checkable.
